text:
claire: Quick flag — noticed a steady uptick in cross-region egress from eu-central tenants to us-east S3. Warm pool is getting fragmented with lots of 1-2 slot allocations.
tom: Saw a 1.9x increase in cross-region bytes on Saturday night. Warm-slice count per-tenant is up and allocator isn't coalescing because of affinity scoring. Link: https://telemetry.internal/graphs?panel=warm_slices
isabella: Can you paste the allocation profile? is this mostly short bursts causing the allocator to treat them as persistent?
claire: Profile: many long-lived tiny sessions (median duration ~12m) + heavy POST traffic to us-east buckets. Network path goes cross-AZ and sometimes cross-region. Means we can't safely pack them next to other tenants with different egress patterns.
tom: Hypothesis: if we localize S3 backhaul (mirror or endpoint rewrite) for the noisy tenants, allocator coalescing tolerance could be relaxed and reduce slice churn.
infra-bot: recent-alert: slice_churn_rate(eu-central) > 0.7 for 6h; top tenants: org-451, org-762 :warning:
isabella: Two-parter: short-term mitigation and longer-term allocator change. Short-term: deploy a small L4 proxy (s3-proxy-lite) in eu-central that rewrites requests to our regional mirror. That should cut cross-region egress and make traffic local.
emma: I can spin up proxy canary in eu-central-1 rack A. We'll put a per-tenant routing rule via headers: X-Backhaul-Target: regional-mirror.
claire: Example nginx proxy snippet we tested in staging: 
```
server {
  listen 8080;
  location / {
    proxy_set_header Host regional-mirror.internal;
    proxy_pass https://regional-mirror.internal.svc.cluster.local;
  }
}
```
tom: Long-term: allocator should tolerate small warm slots coalesced if egress locality label matches. Pseudocode for policy: 
```
policy:
  coalesce_window_seconds: 300
  allow_coalesce_if:
    - slot_size_max: 4
      max_egress_remote_fraction: 0.05
    - egress_locality_match: true
```
isabella: We should be careful about risk: coalescing based on egress-locality could accidentally mix tenants that only occasionally flip mirrors. Suggest rollout plan: 1) guard with per-tenant egress-tag confidence score, 2) canary policy in a single rack, 3) automated rollback if tail-latency increases.
emma: Metrics to add: localized_backhaul_bytes_by_tenant, slot_coalesce_attempts, coalesce_success_rate, tail_p95_latency_by_tenant. I'll add Grafana panels.
lily: (devops): I spun up a job to tag top noisy tenants with egress_local=true for the canary. Will update /etc/tenant-egress-tags.
claire: Can we also throttle the top offenders on the host egress while proxy rolls out? Small shaping prevents link saturation that triggers allocator anti-coalesce.
tom: We used 'tc' rules in staging to cap at 250mbit for a tenant. Command: 
```
# cap tenant egress
tc qdisc add dev eth0 root tbf rate 250mbit burst 32k latency 400ms
iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -m comment --comment "tenant:org-451" -j MARK --set-mark 451
```
emma: I'll template a DaemonSet to apply shaping per tenant metadata. Will emit tenant_egress_shaped_bytes counter.
isabella: Rollout schedule proposal: Monday 06:00 UTC deploy s3-proxy-lite canary in rack eu-central-a for tagged tenants; Tuesday 06:00 UTC enable allocator coalesce policy in same rack; 48h observation windows each. Rollback if coalesce_success_rate < 0.7 or p95 latency increases > 20%.
lily: Noted. I'll prepare infra PR for proxy and RBAC for tenant tag updates.
infra-bot: scheduled-canary: s3-localize-canary -> start Mon 06:00 UTC for 48h.
claire: Action items: lily -> PR for proxy + tenant tags, emma -> daemonset shaping + metrics, isabella + tom -> allocator patch + unit tests, claire -> update cost model and postmortem template.
emma: Image pushed: registry/internal/s3-proxy-lite:20260701. Logs look normal in staging.
tom: I'll open allocator PR 7890 and include feature flag.
isabella: Small reminder: add an alert for unexpected cross-region egress after proxy live. If proxy misroutes, we want immediate rollback.
claire: Thanks all. Keep short updates in this thread. If anyone sees sudden cost uptick, @claire @lily please escalate. :mag:
